texts.preamble: Rohit Kumar (Dar) vs Birjesh (47/19, Gp) on 13 March, 2024 :1: In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No: 405/2019 Rohit Kumar vs. Brijesh & ors. Rohit Kumar S/o Baij Nath R/o Village Areual, Post Guren, District Banda, U.P. at present H. No.A-1-135, J.J. Colony, Madanpur Khadar, New Delhi-110076 ....Petitioner Versus 1. Brijesh S/o Sh. Ram Kishore R/o House no. 1435, Gali no.14, Tugalakabad village, Begali colony, Jaitpur, South Delhi 110044 ....Driver/R-1 2. Kurban Sekh S/o Sh. Lalu Shek R/o House no. Rz-750, Gali no. 13B, Tkd Extn. South New Delhi ....Owner/R2 3. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Page no. 1 of 22 :2: Date of Accident : 31.01.2019 Date of filing of DAR : 28.05.2019 Date of decision : 13.03.2024 Rohit Kumar (Dar) vs Birjesh (47/19, Gp) on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188952175/
texts.facts: The present claim arises out of a detailed accident report (DAR), filed by the police on 28.05.2019, in terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act and the same is treated as a claim petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on receipt of a PCR call on 31.01.2019, HC Krishan Kumar (IO), was informed about an accident to have taken place. Injured informed that on 31.01.2019 at about 04:10 PM, he was traveling in a battery rickshaw number DL-4ER-3922, from Govindpuri Gali no. 13 to Govindpuri Metro Station. When he reached Govindpuri Chawk near Gurdwara Ravidas Marg, the driver of battery rickshaw started driving the rickshaw rash and negligently and suddenly he turned it. Due to this, battery rickshaw turned over and claimant received injury in his left hand. After that someone called 100 number and ambulance took the injured to AIIMS Trauma Center and later to Safdarjung Hospital for treatment. 3. On this complaint, an FIR no. 47/2019 was registered at PS Govindpuri, u/s 279/338 of IPC and 3/181 and 5/180 MV Act and the matter was investigated. It is pursuant to the investigation that a charge sheet u/s 279/338 of IPC and 3/181 and 5/180 MV Act was filed before Ld. MM and a DAR was filed before this MACT No. 405/019 Rohit vs. Brijesh & ors. Page no. 2 of 22 :3: Tribunal. 4. Insurance company/Respondent no. 3 filed its reply while no reply was filed by Respondent no. 1 and Respondent no. 2 despite opportunity. In nutshell, as per reply of Respondent no. 3, petitioner has failed to prove rash and negligent driving by Respondent no. 1. It is further pleaded that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence because of which he was chargesheeted u/s 3/181 & Section 5/180 of MV Act. It is pleaded that the claimant has failed to show that he was working as a labour or that he incurred any medical expenses on his alleged treatment. It is however, admitted that the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent no. 3 vide policy number 2210003118P111679402 from 10.12.2018 to 09.12.2019, issued in favour of Respondent no 2. It is pleaded that such insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation as Respondent no.1/ driver was not holding any valid driving licence, at the time of alleged accident. 5. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 19.08.2019. Rohit Kumar (Dar) vs Birjesh (47/19, Gp) on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188952175/ 2 1. Whether the injured Rohit Kumar suffered injures in a road traffic accident on 31.01.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-4ER-3922 being driven by Respondent no.1, owned by respondent no. 2 and Insured with Respondent no. 3 ? Page no. 3 of 22 2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP 3. Relief. 6. Thereafter, evidence was led by the petitioner by examining himself as PW-1. PW-1 led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A and relied upon 9 photographs of injury (running from page no.1 to 5) as Ex.PW1/1, Medical bills (running from page no. 6 to 48) as Ex.PW1/2, Certified copy of DAR (running from page no. 49 to 145) as Ex.PW1/3 and copy of Aadhar Card of deponent marked as Mark A. PW-1 was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for Respondent no. 3. PW-1 was not cross examined by Respondent no. 1 and Respondent no. 2 despite opportunity. 7. No evidence was led by the Respondent no.1 and Respondent no.2 despite opportunity. Respondent no. 3 examined one Raju, Manager of United India Insurance Company as R3W1. R3W1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.R3W1/A and relied upon certified copy of the original Insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/1, charge sheet Ex.PW1/3, copy of notice dated 01.07.2023 served under Order XII Rule 8 CPC as Ex.R3W1/2 and postal receipts as Ex.R3W1/3. He was not cross examined by the petitioner or Respondent no.1 and Respondent no. 2 despite opportunity. , issue wise findings are as under: 1. In the present case, the injured /petitioner has specifically deposed about accident dated 31.01.2019.
texts.arguments: . Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 10. He has categorically stated that at the time of the accident, offending vehicle bearing no. DL-4ER-3922 was being driven by Respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner. He has deposed that the driver of the MACT No. 405/019 Rohit vs. Brijesh & ors. Page no. 5 of 22 offending Rohit Kumar (Dar) vs Birjesh (47/19, Gp) on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188952175/ 3 vehicle was intoxicated and lost control over the vehicle causing claimant to fall from the vehicle due to which he received grievous injuries. He deposed that he has incurred medical expenses to the tune of Rs.50806/-. He deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle also did not hold a valid driving licence. 11. It has been contended by the respondent no. 3 that the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. respondent no. 1, not only breached the condition of the Insurance policy by driving the offending vehicle without a valid driving licence but also drove the same in an intoxicated condition. As per cross examination of PW-1, no suggestion that the vehicle was not driven in a rash or negligent manner has been put and thus the issue of rash and negligent driving causing the accident leading to injury to the claimant , has not been disputed specifically. 12. Further, petitioner has relied upon photographs of injury Ex.PW1/1 and certified copy of DAR. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge sheet against Respondent no. 1 u/s 279/338 of IPC and MACT No. 405/019 Rohit vs. Brijesh & ors. Page no. 6 of 22 3/181 and 5/180 MV Act which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 14. It may further be noted that in Cholamandalam Insurance Company vs. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. The following observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh And Another Vs. Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited And Others (2018) 7 SCC 558 is relevant to the present facts and quoted as under: MACT No. 405/019 Rohit vs. Brijesh & ors. Page no. 8 of 22 ''...15. We may fruitfully note that the three-Judge Bench adverted to situations where the driver does not have a licence and the same has been allowed to be driven by the owner of the vehicle by such person, the insurer would be entitled to succeed in defence and avoid liability, but the position would be different where the disputed question of fact arises as to whether the driver had a valid licence and where the owner of the vehicle committed a breach of the terms of the contract of insurance as also the provisions of the Act by consciously allowing any person to drive a vehicle who did not have a valid driving licence." It was further observed: ''...24. Nothing has been brought on record by the insured to prove that he had a permit of the vehicle. The said directions are in consonance with the principles stated in Swaran Singh and other cases pertaining to pay and recover principle...''.. 17. In such circumstances, the liability of compensation falls primarily upon the driver as well as the owner of the offending vehicle bearing registration number DL-4ER-3922. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. MACT No. 405/019 Rohit vs. Brijesh & ors. Page no. 9 of 22 Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 18. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and MACT No. 405/019 Rohit vs. Brijesh & ors. Page no. 10 of 22 miscellaneous expenditure; (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising; (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability; (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 18.1. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). 18.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence Rohit Kumar (Dar) vs Birjesh (47/19, Gp) on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188952175/ 6 corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 18.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item MACT No. 405/019 Rohit vs. Brijesh & ors. Page no. 11 of 22 (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 18.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. 18.6. It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 18.7. Hence, the loss of income of the petitioner on account of accident shall be ascertained on the basis of minimum MACT No. 405/019 Rohit vs. Brijesh & ors. Page no. 12 of 22 wages prevalent in State of U.P. at the relevant time. 20. MACT No. 405/019 Rohit vs. Brijesh & ors. Page no. 13 of 22 (v) Loss of income : Since no proof of Rs.7675/- continuous hospitalization or consequent loss of work or employment has been filed, but on the basis of nature of injury, assuming that the claimant would have been incapacitated from working for gain for about one month, compensation under this head has been arrived at on the basis of loss of minimum wages prevalent in U.P. at the relevant time. (vii) Any other loss / expenditure : Not applicable 2. Non-Pecuniary Loss : (ii) Pain and suffering : Compensation Rs.5000/- for pain and suffering is to be awarded keeping in mind the nature of injuries suffered by the njured. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. 26. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the MACT No. 405/019 Rohit vs. Brijesh & ors. Page no. 17 of 22 procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
